entry.reasons: The entry accurately reflects the content of Essential Knowledge 9.1.A.1 regarding the dispersal of matter and entropy changes. The caution correctly warns against using the vague term 'disorder' which is often penalized on the AP Exam in favor of 'dispersal of matter/energy'.

Topic 9.1.A.1 states that “Entropy increases when matter becomes more dispersed,” including the listed phase changes and gas expansion at constant temperature. It also says entropy “generally increases” when gas-phase products have more total moles than gas-phase reactants. The entry preserves that qualification, and its caution appropriately warns against treating the gas-moles rule as absolute.

It also gives the gas-phase rule with the correct direction: products' total moles greater than reactants' total moles.
